statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. NQ front-month extended its overnight high to 29,682.50 and then retraced, leaving a 29,530.50-29,682.50 band about 0.51% wide after roughly ten hours; Investing.com's delayed feed shows 29,663.50 (+0.33%) while Yahoo's shows 29,565.25 (+0.14%). Tail eases one point to 6 because the marginal new high was retraced rather than extended, and because ES (-0.04%) and YM (-0.44%) are negative against a bid NQ, so no aligned index trend exists. Stress rises to 56 with Brent at $97.37 (+1.1%) and WTI at $92.57 (+1.2%) on weekend US-Iran strikes around the Strait of Hormuz, the 10-year near 4.784% and market-implied odds of a 16 September Fed hike at 58%. US cash equity and Treasury markets are closed for Labor Day and CME equity futures halt near 17:00 UTC before reopening at 22:00 UTC.
recommendation: Conditions map to EA_ON for NQ futures and NAS100 CFD, and Tail remains far below the block threshold. Conditional risk concentrates in the narrow 15:00-17:00 UTC window covering the European cash close into the Labor Day futures halt, and secondarily at the 22:00 UTC restart for the Tuesday trade date, rather than across the whole outlook. Every forecast hour maps below the block threshold. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures retrace a marginal new high as an AI-chip rally in Asia meets rising oil and a closed US cash session on Labor Day
body:
The observation that changed this hour is what happened after the high. The overnight band high extended again, from 29,643.00 to 29,682.50, but price did not hold there: Yahoo's delayed feed now shows 29,565.25, roughly 117 points below the extreme, while Investing.com shows 29,663.50. A new high that is retraced is the opposite of the amplifier that matters for this strategy, so Tail eases one point to 6. The band now runs 29,530.50 to 29,682.50, about 152 points or 0.51%, and has contained roughly ten hours of trade with repeated two-way movement rather than shallow pullbacks.

The cross-asset picture argues the same way. NQ is up about 0.27% while ES is -0.04% and YM is -0.44%, so there is no aligned index trend to extend. The strength is narrow and identifiable: Asian memory and semiconductor names rallied hard, with SK Hynix +6.1%, Kioxia +7.6%, Samsung +4% and TSMC +1.5%, after OpenAI unveiled GPT-6 Astra and revived AI-infrastructure expectations. Latest-session US sector data shows the same split, with semiconductors broadly higher while software and several megacaps were lower. Narrow leadership against divergent index futures reduces directional conviction; it does not create a no-retracement path.

Stress rises two points to 56. Brent is $97.37, up 1.1% and near three-month highs after almost 8% last week, and WTI is $92.57, up 1.2%, following tit-for-tat US and Iranian attacks on vessels in the Strait of Hormuz over the weekend, with Tehran signalling a restricted zone and a new Oman-agreed shipping route. Rates are hawkish rather than calm: the 10-year sits near 4.784%, close to its highest since late 2023, and markets price 58% odds of a Federal Reserve hike on 16 September with 70% for October after August payrolls came in at 162,000. Rising oil, rising yields and rising tech is a genuine tension, and tension of that kind belongs in Stress.

Confidence eases a point to 85. The evidence base is strong, with verified oil levels, a verified Asian session, a verified catalyst and a verified calendar, but the two delayed futures feeds disagree on the last print, and VIX at 14.53 and the H.15 curve are Friday values because US cash markets are shut. The structural features of the day are fixed: no US cash equity or Treasury session, a CME equity-futures halt near 17:00 UTC, five closed hours, and a 22:00 UTC restart for the Tuesday trade date. The danger window stays at 15:00-17:00 UTC, where the European cash close pushes size into a thin holiday book with no US backstop ahead of a hard stop. Mapped policy state remains EA_ON and Tail stays well below the block threshold in every forecast hour.

lookbackSummary: Twenty-three of the 24 preceding hourly Claude assessments are available; the 21:00 UTC hour on 6 September has no published assessment and is marked unavailable with null fields. Tail held a flat 5 through the closed-venue Sunday session, mapping to EA_ON and green in every available hour, stepped to 8 at the 22:00 UTC restart to carry reopen-gap risk, eased back to 5 once that restart proved orderly, and lifted to 7 in the most recent hour when the overnight high extended and price sat near the band extreme. Stress moved through a 52 to 60 band, peaking at 60 into the Sunday close before easing to 54 across the Asian session. Confidence stayed in a narrow 84 to 86 range throughout. Dominant mode was normal in every available hour.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours cover the remainder of the European morning traded against closed US cash equity and Treasury markets on Labor Day, a shortened futures session that halts near 17:00 UTC, five closed hours, the 22:00 UTC restart for the Tuesday trade date, and the Tuesday Asian session. Conditional Tail stays inside the low band in every hour: 6 for the current hour and the next, 7 across the European mid and late morning where holiday-thinned depth and live Hormuz headlines meet real book depth without a US cash backstop, 6 through the holiday-thinned afternoon that has no cash open, 8 in the flagged 15:00-17:00 UTC window covering the European close into the halt, 5 falling to 4 across the closed hours, 8 at the 22:00 UTC restart for reopen-gap risk, and 7 easing to 6 through the Tuesday Asian session. Stress runs 55 to 58 while the venue is open, steps down to 46 to 50 across the halt, and returns to 55 to 57 after the restart. Confidence decays from 85 to 70 as the distance from current price evidence grows. Every hour maps to EA_ON and green. The week's principal checkpoints are Thursday's PPI and Friday's CPI, both at 12:30 UTC.
